title: Voice the feedback for early readers
statement: In an early-reading course, voice every corrective and confirming feedback line, because the learner who most needs the correction is the one least able to read it.
example: A survey found 56% of one build's generated voice clips had no playback site, and every corrective feedback line was silent.
detail: A survey of a Grade 3 reading build on 2026-07-29 found 56% of its generated voice clips had no playback site, and while the story and the teaching narration were voiced, every piece of corrective feedback was silent, which its schema calls exactly backwards. The rule now voices the narration that teaches, the corrective and confirming feedback, which renders after the child acts and so gives nothing away, and the modelled answers, since nothing is assessed while the child watches. Question stems, instructions and prompts are never voiced, because reading the task is part of the assessed skill.

evidence.quote: the reverse assertion: every **generated** clip has a playback site (56% did not, once)
which is exactly backwards: the child who most needs the correction is the one least
it renders *after* the child acts, so voicing it gives nothing away
reading the task is part of the assessed skill
